text:
ana: FYI spotted a few invoice-preview mismatches — small number of usage records landed after preview snapshot. Looks like enrich backfill completed late and our compact aggregation committed afterwards.
chuck: ah, the late-arrival pattern again. Which tenants are impacted?
priya: quick query to find suspects: ```sql
SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) late_count
FROM billing.raw_events
WHERE received_at BETWEEN '2025-04-02T02:00:00Z' AND '2025-04-02T03:00:00Z'
AND committed_at > preview_snapshot_time
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY late_count DESC
LIMIT 100;
```
ben: can we avoid surprising customers? I suggest adding a non-blocking banner on invoice preview: "Preview generated at X; recent events may still be pending" with a link to details.
nana: (typo) ana: ^^ agreed. Product won't like slowing previews for all customers with stricter watermarks.
chuck: Instead of delaying, surface a "watermark_age" metric next to preview timestamp and a computed "late_rate" for the tenant. That helps CS triage.
priya: late_rate can be derived at read time: late_events / total_events in the last window. No change to event schema.
ben: ops: can we run a one-off backfill to apply missing credits? Make it idempotent — we burned ourselves on a double-apply last quarter.
ops-bot: backfill request accepted: job billing_backfill_20250402_02 queued. ETA ~20m. Will post  progress.
chuck: how about the internal API knobs? Customers asked for per-tenant dedupe-window customization. If we allow that, invoice previews become inconsistent across tenants.
priya: let's avoid per-tenant toggles initially. Offer per-plan defaults (starter/pro/enterprise) and revisit if there's real demand.
nana: ana: also want to add a small telemetry counter from the aggregator: events_arriving_post_snapshot so we can alert before preview runs.
ben: good idea. We can add a KQL alert: if events_arriving_post_snapshot / window_count > 0.01 for > 5m -> create ticket (non-pager) and if > 0.05 -> page oncall.
chuck: for the backfill idempotency, simplest approach: tag each applied credit with source_backfill_run_id and only apply if not present. Pseudocode: ```python
for e in events:
    key = f"backfill:{run_id}:{e.id}"
    if ledger.exists(key):
        continue
    ledger.insert_credit(e.tenant, e.amount, metadata={"backfill_run": run_id})
```
priya: also include a checksum of event fields to avoid edge-case duplicates when IDs change.
ops-bot: backfill started. Shards: 0/8. Progress: 50% after 10m.
billing-bot: alert: preview delta > $2000 for 6 tenants, tickets BILL-1100..BILL-1105 auto-created.
nana: ana: I'll draft a polite notification for affected tenants with a link to the preview + explanation.
chuck: follow-ups capture: (1) UI banner + watermark_age display (2) tenant late_rate metric in console (3) aggregator telemetry counter + alert rule (4) idempotent backfill pattern + ledger audit (5) product decision on per-plan vs per-tenant dedupe config.
priya: I'll own the late_rate metric. Chuck + Ben pair on the backfill idempotency PR. Ana will handle the UI banner.
ops-bot: backfill completed: success. 8/8 shards. Applied 427 credits, skipped 12 duplicates. Report: https://console.internal/billing/backfill/1759990000
ben: after-action: let's add a short dashboard card for real-time watermark_age and a small note on invoice preview page about potential late events.
chuck: also file a tiny RFC explaining why previews are eventually-consistent and how watermarks work for support. I'll author it.
nana: ana: thanks everyone. tagging for retro and keeping the thread for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
